newsitem.title: USA: Fed well aware of CPI biases, Lindsey says.
newsitem.headline: Fed well aware of CPI biases, Lindsey says.

text.p: A finding by an independent commission that the U.S. Consumer Price Index substantially overstates inflation came as no surprise to the Federal Reserve, Fed Governor Lawrence Lindsey said Thursday.
"It's not news," Lindsey told reporters after a speech to the Consumer Federation of America.
Still, he praised the work of the five-member congressionally appointed commission led by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin, saying it had carefully set out the issue and quantified it.

The panel concluded that the CPI was overstated by 1.1 percentage points, a problem that it said was costing the federal government billions of dollars because of inaccurate indexing of federal benefits and tax brackets.
The Boskin commission recommended several steps to remedy the problem, including potential legislation to change the way the benefit programs and taxes are indexed.

Lindsey said the report indicated that some problems with the CPI can be fixed by technicians at the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics but others "are inherent in the nature of the CPI and will require legislative change."
